claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy is a single-phase solid-solution refractory high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Controlled minor alloying and thermomechanical processing can create an approximately 10 vol% ductile BCC second phase, such as an Nb-rich phase, in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed processing can encourage phase separation without drastically altering high-temperature stability.
At strain rates of at least 10^3 s^-1, deformation is adiabatic, thermal softening is prominent, and conventional strain hardening is limited.
The intervention will produce a hard refractory-HEA matrix interspersed with ductile second-phase particles or regions.
The ductile second phase will provide preferential sites for strain partitioning and enhanced local work hardening.
The ductile phase will redistribute local stress and enhance load sharing during rapid deformation.
Stress redistribution and load sharing will delay shear-band formation.
The dual-phase structure will dissipate energy more effectively and thereby retard strain localization under adiabatic heating.
The modified alloy will have higher dynamic yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will sustain more than 15% uniform strain before localization under high-rate dynamic loading.
The modified alloy will exhibit enhanced impact-energy absorption.
The benefits are expected primarily during adiabatic deformation at strain rates of at least 10^3 s^-1.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can retain exceptional mechanical performance at temperatures above 800 °C and, in some cases, up to 1500 °C.
The introduced second phase may compromise the phase stability of the HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and conditions attribute rapid failure to high-rate adiabatic deformation, but the predicted-outcome field calls rapid failure a behavior of the quasi-static baseline. The stated baseline provides only quasi-static property values and does not establish rapid dynamic failure.

The prediction concerns uniform strain before localization, whereas the measurement list parenthetically equates that quantity with fracture strain. Uniform strain and total fracture strain are distinct and need not give the same result.
